title: Your stock ends flat. You still lose 22.1%.

fact.thing: hypothetical one-year loss of a 2x single-stock ETF when the stock ends flat at 50% volatility
fact.box: LongPoint SavvyLong (2X) single-stock ETFs on the TSX (AAPU, AMZU, ALPU, MSFU, NVDU, TSLU)
fact.claim: LongPoint's prospectus for its Canadian 2x single-stock ETFs gives an example: a stock ends a year exactly where it started, with 50% annualized volatility. The 2x ETF would be expected to lose 22.1% over that year. At 25% volatility the loss is 6%, so the bigger the daily swings, the bigger the loss. The figures are hypothetical, cover one year rather than one month, are before fees and expenses, and are not a forecast.
sources: LONGPOINT SAVVYLONG PROSPECTUS (LONG TERM PERFORMANCE RISK)

felt.how: $1,000 in a 2x single-stock ETF vs what's left after one flat year at 50% swings

sources.label: LONGPOINT SAVVYLONG PROSPECTUS (PRICE VOLATILITY RISK)
sources.what: If a respective common stock provided no return over a one-year period and experienced annualized volatility of 50%, the hypothetical loss for a one-year period for a Double Single Stock ETF rises to 22.1% (as shown in Table 1 below).

sources.label: LONGPOINT SAVVYLONG PROSPECTUS (LONG TERM PERFORMANCE RISK)
sources.what: For periods longer than a single day, the Double Single Stock ETFs will typically decline in value if the return of the respective common stock is flat, it is even possible that a SavvyLong ETF can decline in value even if the return of the respective common stock is positive over a period longer than a single day and that a SavvyShort ETF can decline in value even if the return of the respective common stock is negative over a period longer than a single day.
